build_common_tools_justification: Build uses standard ecosystem tooling: npm/vite/tsc for the TypeScript/React frontend and Cargo for the Rust backend, per onrecord-studio/package.json and onrecord-studio/src-tauri/Cargo.toml.
build_floss_tools_justification: All build tools (npm, vite, tsc, cargo, rustc, tauri-cli) are FLOSS; no proprietary compiler/toolchain is required per onrecord-studio/package.json devDependencies and Cargo.toml.
test_justification: Automated FLOSS test suites exist: 5 Vitest suites under onrecord-studio/src/tests/ (App.test.tsx, crawlSettings.test.tsx, crypto.test.ts, ingestion.test.ts, provenanceShield.test.tsx, 860 lines total) and 29 `#[test]` functions across onrecord-studio/src-tauri/src plus onrecord-studio/src-tauri/tests/bench_migration.rs. How to run them is documented in onrecord-studio/README.md's 'Quality gate' section (`cargo test ...`, `npx vitest run`) and as npm scripts ('test', 'test:unit') in package.json.
test_invocation_justification: Tests run via standard per-language invocations: `npm run test:unit` (vitest run) for TypeScript and `cargo test --workspace --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml` for Rust, both documented in onrecord-studio/package.json scripts and README.md.
test_most_justification: onrecord-studio/package.json includes @vitest/coverage-v8 as a devDependency but onrecord-studio/vitest.config.ts defines no coverage thresholds or enforced coverage gate, and no coverage report was generated to verify branch/functionality coverage, so 'most' coverage cannot be confirmed.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: onrecord-studio/.github/workflows/ci.yml runs on push to main and on every pull_request; the 'checks' job runs IPC contract/tsc/eslint and the 'rust' job runs `cargo test --workspace` on ubuntu/macos/windows matrix.
test_policy_justification: onrecord-studio/docs/comment-policy.md states explicitly: 'A SECURITY: comment must have a nearby test. This is the rule with teeth.' Root CLAUDE.md also states 'Every new test for one of these guards must be proven by temporarily removing the guard and showing the failure,' documenting a policy that new/critical functionality gets tests.
tests_are_added_justification: Commit 5dd9385 ('feat: wire crawl and pacing settings into the source composer', `git show --stat 5dd9385`) adds both onrecord-studio/src/utils/crawlPolicy.ts (new functionality) and onrecord-studio/src/tests/crawlSettings.test.tsx (109 lines) in the same commit, showing the policy is followed in recent history.
tests_documented_added_justification: The testing requirement is documented in onrecord-studio/docs/comment-policy.md ('A SECURITY: comment must have a nearby test') rather than only informally practiced.
warnings_justification: onrecord-studio/.github/workflows/ci.yml sets `RUSTFLAGS: -D warnings` and runs `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; ESLint is run via `eslint . --max-warnings 0` in package.json's 'lint' script, using onrecord-studio/eslint.config.js (@eslint/js recommended + typescript-eslint recommended).
warnings_fixed_justification: CI treats warnings as build failures (`-D warnings` for Rust, `--max-warnings 0` for ESLint), so any warning blocks merges to main, per onrecord-studio/.github/workflows/ci.yml.
warnings_strict_justification: Rust uses default clippy lints (not `clippy::pedantic`/`clippy::nursery`) and ESLint uses the 'recommended' rule sets (eslint.configs.recommended, typescript-eslint recommended) rather than a strict/type-checked config, per onrecord-studio/eslint.config.js and onrecord-studio/.github/workflows/ci.yml — not the maximally strict setting available.
know_secure_design_justification: onrecord-studio/docs/architecture.md section 5 ('Security model') documents the IPC trust-boundary design explicitly: 'each command body is the trust boundary... Validation belongs there, not in the manifest,' plus the CSP policy (no unsafe-eval, no unsafe-inline scripts) and known-gaps analysis (ingest_local_files path handling). This is direct evidence of secure-design reasoning by the primary developer.
know_common_errors_justification: The codebase has 16 inline `SECURITY(...)` boundary comments (e.g. onrecord-studio/src/utils/crypto.ts parseDidWeb: 'A validation boundary, not a convenience parser... Rejections are pinned in src/tests/crypto.test.ts') addressing untrusted-input handling, plus docs/architecture.md noting 'All parser input is untrusted: documents arrive from arbitrary government portals.' This shows awareness of injection/untrusted-input classes of errors relevant to this software.
crypto_published_justification: Crypto usage is limited to published standards: TLS via rustls (reqwest with `default-features=false, features=["rustls",...]` in onrecord-studio/src-tauri/Cargo.toml), SHA-256 via the `sha2` crate, and the published C2PA specification via the `c2pa` crate (0.90.15) with `rust_native_crypto` feature. No custom/home-grown crypto protocol found.
crypto_call_justification: Cargo.toml dependencies show calls to dedicated crypto libraries (rustls via reqwest, sha2, c2pa) rather than reimplementation; no hand-rolled cipher/hash code was found under onrecord-studio/src-tauri/src.
crypto_floss_justification: All crypto-related dependencies (rustls, sha2, c2pa with rust_native_crypto) are FLOSS Rust crates, per onrecord-studio/src-tauri/Cargo.toml.
crypto_keylength_justification: TLS is handled by rustls (reqwest 'rustls' feature in Cargo.toml), which by default only negotiates modern cipher suites/key exchange (e.g. X25519, P-256/P-384, RSA >=2048) meeting current NIST minimums; the app does not itself generate or configure smaller key lengths anywhere in src-tauri/src.
crypto_working_justification: rustls does not implement SSLv2/SSLv3, MD4/MD5, single-DES, RC4, or Dual_EC_DRBG, and the app uses `sha2` (SHA-256) rather than MD5 for content hashing (onrecord-studio/src/utils/crypto.ts isSha256Hex/isSha256Base64), so no broken default algorithm is depended on.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 usage found in crypto code (grep of src/utils/crypto.ts and src-tauri/src shows SHA-256 only); the app has no SSH component, so CBC-in-SSH does not apply.
crypto_pfs_justification: rustls (used via reqwest's 'rustls' feature) defaults to ECDHE-based key exchange for TLS 1.2 and always uses forward-secret key exchange in TLS 1.3, giving perfect forward secrecy by default.
crypto_password_storage_justification: N/A: the application is a local desktop tool with no user-account/password system; grep for 'password'/'argon2'/'bcrypt'/'pbkdf2' across src and src-tauri/src found only URL-credential parsing/rejection code (e.g. onrecord-studio/src-tauri/src/ingestion/client.rs checks `url.password().is_some()` to reject credentialed URLs), not password storage.
crypto_random_justification: N/A: the application does not itself generate cryptographic keys or nonces; `uuid` (v4) is used for non-cryptographic identifiers and TLS randomness is delegated entirely to rustls internally.
delivery_mitm_justification: No public delivery/download mechanism exists yet: the repo has never been published, and no release artifacts have been distributed, so there is nothing to confirm is served over HTTPS/SSH.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No release/delivery mechanism exists yet to evaluate (see delivery_mitm_status); this cannot be confirmed as compliant until a real distribution channel exists.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: onrecord-studio/.github/workflows/ci.yml runs an 'audit' job on every push/PR (`npm audit --audit-level=high` and `rustsec/audit-check@v2`), and onrecord-studio/.cargo/audit.toml documents the only ignored advisories as unreachable transitive GTK3/unic-* issues with no available upgrade, re-reviewed per Tauri version bump. No evidence of any unaddressed medium+ vulnerability sitting open.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: The same CI audit job (onrecord-studio/.github/workflows/ci.yml 'audit') fails the build on any high/critical advisory not explicitly ignored in onrecord-studio/.cargo/audit.toml, giving rapid detection/fix pressure for critical issues.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Searched for 'api_key'/'secret_key'/'private_key'/PEM private-key headers across src, src-tauri, and .github with grep; the only match was onrecord-studio/src-tauri/src/ingestion/source_catalog.rs's `AccessRequirement::ApiKeyOrAccount` enum variant (a connector-metadata label, not a credential value). No actual key/secret material found.

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: Only default clippy lints are run; no vulnerability-focused static analyzer (e.g. CodeQL, Semgrep, clippy security lint groups) is configured in onrecord-studio/.github/workflows/ci.yml.

static_analysis_often_justification: onrecord-studio/.github/workflows/ci.yml triggers clippy on every push to main and every pull_request, i.e. on every commit reaching CI.
